newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss purchasing index rises slightly in December.
newsitem.headline: Swiss purchasing index rises slightly in December.

text.p: The Swiss purchasing managers' index (PMI) compiled by Credit Suisse and the Swiss Association for Material Management and Purchasing (SVME) rose 0.2 percentage points in December to 44.3 percent from a revised 44.1 percent in November.
The November index was previously reported at 44.4 percent.
The employment sub-index, at 42.4, was at its lowest level since the PMI was first compiled in September 1995.
All eight sub-indices remained below 50 percent, indicating a contraction.
The categories are production, orders on hand, purchasing volume, purchasing prices, delivery times, inventory purchases, inventory sales and employment.
Besides employment, the sub-indices production, inventory sales also showed declines.
Orders on hand, purchasing volume, purchasing prices, delivery times and inventory purchases rose.
Prices were up mainly in the area of plastics, while prices fell for various metals and electronic components.
The Swiss PMI is based on surveys in which companies are asked to rate each sub-index as higher, lower or unchanged from the month before.
